messages.subject: Behavior of 'stratifyBy' for exon array
parts:
Hi,
I've been trying to adapt the fit function for exon arrays for something
I want to do, and I have run into a strange error for a particular unit.
What happens is that the dimension of the intensity matrix for the unit
is different if I do readUnits(plm) versus readUnits(getDataSet(plm)) --
11 rows versus 22, so MORE with the original data than with the plm.
There are no groups, so this isn't because of the mergeGroups=T issue.
What seems to be happening is at the level of 'getCellIndices' in the
readUnits command. The getCellIndices.ProbeLevelModel function is
returning 11 cell indices instead of the 22 in the original data because
of the stratifyBy="pm" command in getCellIndices.AffymetrixCdfFile. What
I don't understand is why this is happening -- there are no MMs in the
exon arrays, I thought.

By the way, this is the 4100+ unit that the program has cycled through
and the first time I got this error. (Ken, this is the Breast Cancer
Cell Line data, unit 21973).

Thanks,
Elizabeth

P.S. My personal error is downstream because I ignored the stratifyBy
option at some point to get CellIndices, and so my vector of Ids for
each of the probes is length 22 instead of 11 and I'm getting a problem.
I can fix this, but I would like to know why it is doing this before I do.

> getCellIndices(getCdf(getDataSet(plm)),units=errorUnit)
$`4056650`

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Behavior of 'stratifyBy' for exon array
parts:
> I've been trying to adapt the fit function for exon arrays for something
> I want to do, and I have run into a strange error for a particular unit.

> of the stratifyBy="pm" command in getCellIndices.AffymetrixCdfFile. What
> I don't understand is why this is happening -- there are no MMs in the
> exon arrays, I thought.

There are some generic MMs, but these are not generally (to the best of my
knowledge) mixed in with PMs inside units.

> By the way, this is the 4100+ unit that the program has cycled through
> and the first time I got this error. (Ken, this is the Breast Cancer
> Cell Line data, unit 21973).
What exon or transcript ID does this correspond to?

Just going by the indices, it DOES look like you have MMs here (index one
higher than PMs). What does

cdf <- getCdf(getDataSet(plm))
readCdfUnits(cdf, units=errorUnit)

give?

Cheers,

Ken

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Behavior of 'stratifyBy' for exon array
parts:
> The transcript ID is `4056650` and there is only 1 exon so it seems to
> have the same Id (though for some reason I thought that shouldn't
> happen...that it would still get a unique probeset ID)

The convention seems to be that when there is just one exon, it has the
same ID as the transcript cluster.

You definitely have MMs there - these are probes for which pbase
(13th base of probe) is the same as tbase (13th base of target) instead of
being complementary. I've tried looking up unit 4056650 but it isn't on
netaffx, nor is it in the gff annotation files, but for some reason it is
in the metaprobeset files (.mps) that I got from

http://www.affymetrix.com/Auth/analysis/downloads/na20/exon/HuEx-1_0-st-v2.r2.dt1.hg18.zip

Cheers.

Ken
